delta.text: Not related to the com
parison logic. This confirms none of the intervening commits touched the `<=` comparison — it stayed unchanged from `9dc7503` until the fix in

`6188513`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 9dc75038618786d
9e4ae64b84a8f6ce7

cff2d075

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the full history of `BookView.java`'s `getPage
NumberFor()` method (the function touched by the fix commit) using `git log -p --follow`. I located every point where `int
pageNum = 0;` was introduced/changed, and cross-referenced the debug log string `"Looking for pageNumber for index="` that appears in the fix
ed method to find the commit that gave the method its current shape. I then examined how the returned `pageNumber` is consumed downstream, in `ReadingFrag

ment.java`:
```java
if (config.isShowPageNumbers() && pageNumber > 0) {
    ... display page number ...
}
```
So a page number of `0` (or neg

ative) is treated as "don't display a page number" — appropriate for a title page, which shouldn't show "page 1".

**(2) The intro
ducing change:** Commit `9dc75038618786d9e4ae64b84a8f6ce7cff2d075` ("Fixed page-number calculation.", Aug 5 2013) rewrote the off

set-counting loop and, critically, changed the comparison operator:
```diff
-  for ( int i=0; i < offsets.size() && offsets.get(i) < position
ically `0`), this changed the loop condition from `0 < 0` (false, loop skipped, `pageNum` stays at its init value `0`) to `0 <= 0` (true
, loop executes once, `pageNum` becomes `1`). That turns the title page's page number from `0` (hidden by the `pageNumber > 0` check) into `1` (incorrectly displayed as a

real page).

**(3) Evidence:**
